reader.decision: Correct my summary: the key gets the negotiated format (avif, webp or orig), not the whole Accept header. Then hand Petra the two edits: negotiate must run before lookup, and the key carries the format.
reader.decision_reason: The message confirms my cause and current-key statements but shows my fix summary was wrong. A raw Accept key would split the cache into 1,912 variants, while the negotiated format has only three values.

reconstruction.problem: img-edge caches images under path and query string only. A WebP image cached after a Chrome request is served to Safari 13, which cannot decode WebP, so the image is broken.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Safari 13 users get WebP bytes and see broken images. Also, negotiate runs after lookup in serve_image, so cache_key cannot see the format today.
reconstruction.fix: In edge/handler.py, serve_image calls negotiate first and passes image_format to lookup and save. In edge/cache.py, cache_key(request, image_format) appends the format to the path-and-query string, and lookup and save take image_format and pass it on.
reconstruction.cost: Two small edits in two files. Using the format gives three key values. A raw Accept header would give 1,912 variants and lower the hit rate. Any other cost is not stated.

reader.closing_answer: Not right in full. The first and third points are right: today's key is path and query only, and Safari 13 cannot decode WebP. The second is wrong: the key gets the negotiated format (avif, webp or orig), not the whole Accept header. I correct that, then hand Petra the two edits, with negotiate running before lookup.
